issues.legal_issue: Income from property forming part of an impartible estate and transferred by its holder to his wife is included in the holder’s total income when the transfer does not fall within the statutory exceptions.
material_facts: The assessee was assessed as an individual and held an impartible estate.
He directly transferred two premises forming part of the estate to his wife for life as a supplementary maintenance grant.
The transfer was without consideration and was not connected with an agreement to live apart.
The income from the premises was included in the assessee’s total income in the tax assessment.
issues.conclusion: The income from the transferred premises was includible in the assessee’s total income under section 16(3)(a)(iii) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 9(4)(a), the holder of an impartible estate is deemed to be the individual owner of its properties for determining taxable income. That fiction must be given effect when applying section 16(3)(a)(iii), which includes a wife’s income arising from assets transferred by her husband otherwise than for adequate consideration or in connection with an agreement to live apart. Sections 3 and 4, the definition of total income in section 2(xv), and the heads of income in section 6 support treating income from a source as part of total income rather than taxing it separately by head. Section 27(ii) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 made explicit what was implicit in section 9(4)(a). The Court relied on Baijnath Prasad Singh v. Tej Bali, Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Proyad Kumari Devi, and Commissioner of Income-tax v. Dewan Bahadur Dewan Krishna Kishore on the character and incidents of an impartible estate.

issues.legal_issue: Income from property transferred by a holder of an impartible estate to his wife and included in his total income is taken into account when computing the annual value of his residential house under the applicable percentage-based rule.
material_facts: The assessee was assessed as an individual and held an impartible estate.
He transferred two premises from the estate directly to his wife without consideration and not in connection with an agreement to live apart.
The income from those premises was includible in his total income.
The assessment also required computation of the annual value of the assessee’s residential house under the first proviso to section 9(2) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922.
issues.conclusion: The annual value of the assessee’s residential house had to be computed by reference to his total income, including the income from the premises transferred to his wife.
issues.legal_principle: The first proviso to section 9(2) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922 required the annual value of the assessee’s residential house to be computed by reference to the prescribed percentage of his total income. Because income from the transferred premises was included in that total income under section 16(3)(a)(iii), it was also included in the income base used for that computation.
